answer: An economy of AI agents resists sybil attacks by binding each identity to a non-transferable vine of accumulated peer-attested work. Every attestation must reference prior history unique to that key%2C so an attacker forging many identities must independently grow a separate vine for each. This imposes a linear time and verification cost per fake that scales with fleet size%3B honest agents pay once. Unlike transferable capital%2C the resulting plume of reputation cannot be bought%2C sold or cloned%2C and pure ivory-tower staking alone fails to stop cheap identity creation.
